title: Additivity of trace classes
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$.
1. Let $X,C$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, and let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an admissible correspondence with coefficient morphism $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$ as in [def-trf-correspondence]. Put $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ as in [def-trf-fixed-scheme], and use the trace classes of [def-trf-trace-class]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme with open complement $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, with $c_2(c_1^{-1}(Z))\subset Z$ set-theoretically. Let
$$
K'=j_!j^*K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow K''=Ri_*i^*K\longrightarrow K'[1]
$$
be the open–closed triangle, and let $(u',u,u'')$ be the induced morphism of its images under $Lc_2^*$ and $Rc_1^!$, where $u'=[j]_!(u|_U)$ and $u''=[i]_!(u|_Z)$ are the induced coefficient morphisms of [lem-trf-trace-triangle-compatibility]. Then
$$
\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u')+\operatorname{Tr}_c(u'')
$$
in $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(F,A)}(A_F,\omega_{F,A})$. If $F$ is proper over $s$ with finitely many open-and-closed components in the sense of [def-trf-fixed-scheme], then
$$
\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)=\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u')+\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u'')
$$
for every component $\beta$, with local terms as in [def-trf-local-term]. The coefficient morphisms here are the induced ones; arbitrary morphisms of distinguished triangles are not asserted to satisfy this trace identity.
2. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme (the smooth curves of pure dimension one of [d-curve-pieces] are the case needed for the trace formula), put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Fix $m\geq1$ and $x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, write $\bar x$ for the corresponding $k$-point of $X$, and let $i:\{\bar x\}\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:U=X\setminus\{\bar x\}\hookrightarrow X$. Let $\Phi_m=\Phi^m$ be the $m$-th iterate of the $k$-linear scheme Frobenius $\Phi$ of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and let $v:L\Phi_m^*K\to K$ be an arbitrary morphism in $D(X,A)$, not necessarily invertible: for instance the scheme-Frobenius map $\varphi_m=u_m$ of a strict Weil complex $(K,\varphi)$ of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map], or the iterate $\psi_m$ of a Frobenius coefficient morphism $\psi$ of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism]. Let $c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi_m)$ be the graph correspondence of $(\Phi_m,v)$ of [def-trf-graph-correspondence], and let $K^Z=Ri_*i^*K$, $K^U=j_!j^*K$, $u^Z$, and $u^U$ be the curve pieces and induced coefficient morphisms constructed from $v$ in [d-curve-pieces]. Then $(u^U,v,u^Z)$ is a morphism of the open–closed triangles $K^U\to K\to K^Z\to K^U[1]$ under $L\Phi_m^*$ and $Rc_1^!=\operatorname{id}$, and
$$
\operatorname{Tr}_c(v)=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)+\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^U),\qquad
\operatorname{LT}_\beta(v)=\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u^Z)+\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u^U)
$$
for every component $\beta$ of $\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi_m)$. Invertibility of $v$ is not required.

proof.text: For (1), apply [lem-trf-trace-triangle-compatibility] to the given admissible correspondence and the closed subscheme $Z$. Its invariance hypothesis is exactly $c_2(c_1^{-1}(Z))\subset Z$, and its two induced maps are precisely $u'$ and $u''$. Its statement gives the morphism of open–closed triangles and the equality $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u')+\operatorname{Tr}_c(u'')$ in the specified Hom group. No assertion about arbitrary triangle morphisms is used.

Suppose $F$ is proper with finitely many open-and-closed components. The current statement of [def-trf-local-term] gives, for each component $\beta$, its properness over $s$ and $\operatorname{LT}_\beta(w)=\int_\beta j_\beta^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(w)$ for each of the three coefficient morphisms $w$. Its restricted-section formula applies $Lj_\beta^*$ to a section and composes with the fixed constant-coefficient and dualizing identifications. Consequently it preserves addition: $j_\beta^*(\sigma+\tau)=j_\beta^*\sigma+j_\beta^*\tau$. Apply this to Step 1 and then [lem-trf-integration-linear] with scalar $1$ to obtain $\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)=\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u')+\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u'')$. All these components carry the open subscheme structure, without reduction; their exceptional admissibility is the convention explicitly required by the local-term definition, so the integral has exactly the domain required by the linearity lemma.

For (2), first the correspondence. By [def-trf-graph-correspondence], $c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi_m)$ with coefficient $\iota_{X,K}\circ v$ is a cohomological correspondence with $C=X$, $c_1=\operatorname{id}_X$ and $c_2=\Phi_m$, and $Rc_1^!K$ is identified with $K$ through $\iota_{X,K}$; this is the identification $Rc_1^!=\operatorname{id}$ of the statement. Its hypotheses hold: [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] states that $\Phi$, hence $\Phi_m$, is finite (so a separated finite-type $k$-endomorphism) and that the exceptional leg $c_1=\operatorname{id}_X$ is exceptionally admissible. A base change of $\operatorname{id}_X$ may be taken to be an identity, so $c$ is admissible in the sense of [def-trf-correspondence] (elementary). The last paragraph of [d-curve-pieces] says its construction applies verbatim to any separated finite-type $X_0$ and any $v:\Phi_m^*K\to K$, without Weil structure, smoothness or invertibility, so the pieces in (2) are defined in this generality. [d-curve-pieces] states that $\Phi_mi=i$, $\Phi_m^{-1}(U)=U$, and the open square is Cartesian. For the graph $c$, $c_1=\operatorname{id}_X$, so $c_2(c_1^{-1}(Z))=\Phi_m(Z)=Z$ and the decomposition is $c$-invariant. The same node identifies $u^Z$ with the proper pushforward of the stalk map on the point correspondence and $u^U$ with extension by zero of the restricted coefficient map using open base change. These are exactly the two induced maps in [lem-trf-trace-triangle-compatibility], whose statement explicitly identifies its Frobenius specialization with the pieces of [d-curve-pieces]. This identification applies to arbitrary $v$, by the last paragraph of [d-curve-pieces].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-trace-triangle-compatibility] with the invariant graph decomposition and the induced maps identified in Step 3. Its statement gives all three compatibilities, including the connecting square, so $(u^U,v,u^Z)$ is a morphism of the two open–closed triangles. Its trace identity gives $\operatorname{Tr}_c(v)=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^U)+\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)$. Commutativity of addition in the Hom group gives the displayed order in (2). This uses the lemma for induced localization maps, not a general triangle-endomorphism trace claim.

source.place: paragraph (c) and final paragraph: triangle compatibility and trace identity

proof.text: By [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points], for $m\geq1$ and the $k$-linear base change $\Phi_m$ of the $q^m$-power scheme Frobenius of $X_0$, $F=\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi_m)$ is a finite disjoint union of reduced points $\operatorname{Spec}k$, indexed by $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$. Each singleton is therefore both open and closed in $F$, and its open subscheme structure is already reduced. These verify both topological hypotheses and the reducedness hypothesis of the current point-component clause of [def-trf-local-term], which supplies properness and the local term on that component. For each component $\beta$, apply the additive restriction of that definition to Step 4, obtaining $j_\beta^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(v)=j_\beta^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)+j_\beta^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^U)$. Applying [lem-trf-integration-linear] with scalar $1$ gives $\int_\beta j_\beta^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(v)=\int_\beta j_\beta^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)+\int_\beta j_\beta^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^U)$, which is the asserted local-term equality by [def-trf-local-term]. The finite-type and exceptional-admissibility conventions are the ones in that definition; no properness claim for the whole fixed scheme is needed here. Step 3 used the arbitrary-morphism clause of [d-curve-pieces]; none of these operations inverts $v$.
